profile.headline: Principal Engineer | AI Research Infrastructure @ NVIDIA
profile.summary:
I'm currently a Principal Software Engineer at NVIDIA, helping build out the research infrastructure that supports frontier robotics and physical AI research labs.

In my previous roles, I served as a Tech Lead at Anyscale for three years and as a Software Engineering Manager and Tech Lead at Meta for eight years. My expertise lies in building large-scale developer infrastructure that significantly improves engineering efficiency, including CI/CD, testing, and pre-production (PRE) systems. I led teams that built the backend and infrastructure powering the release of all products at Meta, reducing software release cycles across multiple domains from months to hours. These systems are among the fastest and safest continuous deployment platforms in the industry at Meta’s scale.

positions.title: Principle Engineer
positions.locationName: Santa Clara County, California, United States · On-site
positions.description: Build out the research infrastructure that supports frontier robotics and physical AI research labs 🤖

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Led a multi-quarter transformation of Anyscale’s release model, accelerating Ray releases from a 3-month cadence to weekly, an initiative featured at Ray Summit 2024.
- Re-architected the CI/CD platform end-to-end, including large-scale Ray test parallelization, build caching, automated bisection, and proactive release-blocker detection.
- Drove a company-critical cost-reduction initiative, cutting CI/CD spend by an estimated $10M annually by designing and deploying a predictive test-selection algorithm to optimize compute usage.
- Led the modernization of Ray’s documentation infrastructure, reducing doc build times from 30 minutes to 30 seconds via a Sphinx caching layer, and built a RAG-based AI agent to power customer Q&A over Ray documentation.

Founded and built Anyscale’s Ray data observability dashboard from scratch; it became one of the most widely used internal observability products.

Defined and led the observability strategy for Ray Core, including the launch of Ray One Event System (GitHub #56057), a unified event export platform that replaced multiple legacy systems and was featured at Ray Summit 2025.
- Designed and rolled out the %SAD metric to systematically measure Ray stability and prioritize fixes, resulting in a 3× reduction in stability issues over 6 months.

And lastly, 4-time Anyscale Hackathon winner ❤️
positions.insights: Skills: Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) · System Observability · Ray Core · Amazon Web Services (AWS) · Sphinx · Documentation

positions.title: Engineering Manager
positions.description:
I supported the team building the Continuous Delivery system across Meta, both tactical (operating the releases) and strategic (long-term focus on a faster and safer release platform). Reducing the release cycle and helping every engineers move faster is what we obsess with and what we did - though tooling and advanced automation, we reduced the release cycle of all web from days to hours, mobile from weeks to days, and backend services from months to weeks.

During my time at Meta, I have played several roles from being a Software Engineer, Tech Lead to Engineering Manager, and work on a few things:
- Build out the Release Signals/Automation team through hiring talents, building identity with enduring mission and vision, roadmaps to solve the most important problems for the organization
- Scaled backend release infrastructure and automation across Meta
- Scaled out the fastest continuous web release process for one of the world biggest sites
- Work on infrastructure that powers CI system, testing infrastructure and developer experience

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description: I spent the summer working on an algorithm to reduce the size of test program that are auto-generated by a system called symbolic execution generator. We ended up reduce the size by 50x on average. With previous knowledge working on floating point program at UC Berkeley, I teach the symbolic execution generator to work with test cases that use floating points as primitive types.

positions.title: Graduate Student Researcher
positions.description: Study software testing and symbolic execution. I helped develop a shadow execution for HHVM to run a program using different semantic. One application we did with that system was to optimize floating-point program precision while reducing the memory usage to store bits.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
I studied data mining of software specifications. I built a tool to instrument and trace function call footprints for Java programs and mine common correctness function sequence patterns. I managed to find a few open source bugs that violate the correctness patterns that I found.

I also worked on a technique to mind common patterns from bug fix patches. Using these patterns, we found several bugs in Linux kernel code base that can be benefited from the same patches.

Another data mining technique we did was to mine the differences between traces produced by a working program and a non-working program to localize bugs.

positions.title: Undergraduate Discussion Leader
positions.description: I taught two classes for junior students, one about Java programming and the other is about problem solving and algorithm. Deeply enjoy teaching and mentoring.

positions.title: Undergraduate Student Researcher
positions.description: I added a feature for the Java Pathfinder system, which is a software verification system from Nasa, to verify LTL software specification.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: My first experience working for a customer product. We developed a web-based HR management system for Geylang East Home for the Aged (Geha), replace a bunch of paperwork, spreadsheet book-keeping with automation.

projects.title: Mining of Software API
projects.description: We develop a tool to mine software API sequential rules from execution traces. These rules can be used for software testing purpose.

publications.title: Precimonious: Tuning Assistant for Floating-Point Precision
